label: SYNTHETIC

camera.name: Sony IMX296 1456x1088, 2.5 mm lens, FULL resolution (no binning)

definitions.landmarks: map points under a fixed 3x3 pixel grid according to the PREDICTED pose (9 per frame)
definitions.in_view: the rectified patch (search patch for FINE, template for COARSE*) lies wholly inside the image
definitions.fractions: of in-view landmarks unless the name says otherwise
definitions.correct: accepted, and the matched image pixel back-projected through the TRUE pose lies within 1.5 map pixels of the matched map point
definitions.peak_correct: as correct but ignoring the gates (is the raw NCC maximum at the right place)
definitions.truth_in_window: the true offset is at least one map pixel inside the search window
definitions.mean_ncc_at_truth: best NCC in the 3x3 scores around the true offset, truth-in-window landmarks only
definitions.errors: yaw about the world vertical through the camera, tilt about a horizontal world axis, height as a fraction of true height, position horizontal; random sign/direction per frame, fixed across levels (paired)
definitions.thresholds: tol90_tested is the largest tested level with >=90 % at it and all smaller levels; e50/e90 are linear interpolations; cells with fewer than 20 samples cut the curve

texture.definition: radius at which the 2-D autocorrelation of terrain first falls to 1/e, over 72 directions (unbiased FFT estimate on a 1024 x 1024 grid)

limits: SYNTHETIC. feasibility.terrain is a sum of six sinusoids with wavelengths of about 3.4 to 17 m, not farmland imagery. NCC tolerance depends on the texture correlation length, so the absolute angles will differ on real maps; the scaling (tolerance ~ correlation length / template half-width, both in map pixels) is what should carry over.

A sum of sinusoids is quasi-periodic: the two strongest components (two thirds of the variance) repeat exactly on a lattice of about 16 x 10 m, and each sinusoid equals its own 180 deg rotation up to a shift. Secondary correlation peaks, and therefore every false-match rate reported here, are properties of this texture, not estimates for real imagery.

On the 2 m/px grid the baseline terrain is under-sampled (1/e correlation length about 1.4 map pixels). A sub-pixel misalignment alone then lowers the true peak below the texture repeats inside the search window, so the COARSE and COARSE_WIDE rows measure that artefact, not attitude tolerance. COARSE_TEX4 (wavelengths x4) is the well-sampled coarse case.
Flat ground, pinhole camera, principal point at the image centre, no lens distortion, no blur, no photometric change, no map/season mismatch, 2 grey-level white noise only.
Maps and rectified images are point-sampled (bilinear) with no anti-alias filter.
One error type at a time; real first-fix errors are combined (yaw + tilt + position).

Landmarks are a fixed 3x3 pixel grid projected with the PREDICTED pose (what a real system can do), not pre-selected high-contrast map features. Landmarks within a frame share one pose error, so the nine results per frame are not independent samples.

Thresholds are read from a coarse list of tested error levels and 24 frames per height (12 for COARSE_WIDE); the 90 % level is the largest TESTED level, and the 50 % point is a linear interpolation between tested levels.
Per-landmark gates only (score, peak gap, quadratic peak). No multi-landmark consensus or innovation gating, which the proposal relies on to reject false matches.
